g1.label: 1. The Stone of Destiny … by Edward I
g1.why: Passive, simple past: the stone received the action → was + past participle (seize → seized).

g2.label: 2. William Wallace … Guardian of Scotland
g2.why: Passive, simple past: he was given the title → was + appointed.

g3.label: 3. The Scottish army … at Falkirk
g3.why: Singular subject “army” takes was, not were → was + crushed.

g4.label: 4. Before Bruce became king, Wallace …
g4.why: It happened before another past event → past perfect passive: had (already) been + captured.

g5.label: 5. The Declaration of Arbroath … a statement
g5.why: Still true today → present passive: is + considered.

g6.label: 6. Robert the Bruce … King of Scots
g6.why: Passive, simple past: he received the crown → was + crowned.

g7.label: 7. Scotland’s independence … by England
g7.why: Passive, simple past: independence was recognised by England → was + recognised.

g8.label: 8. The clan system … before Culloden
g8.why: An earlier past state → past perfect passive: had been + weakened.

g1.label: 1. … Wallace won, he couldn’t hold on
g1.why: “Although” opens a concession — a win, but he still couldn’t hold off the English.

g2.label: 2. Edward invaded … forced loyalty

g3.label: 3. Outnumbered … decisive victory
g3.why: “Nevertheless” signals contrast: outnumbered, yet they won.

g4.label: 4. Letter to the Pope … recognition
g4.why: “As a result” shows cause and effect: the letter led to recognition.

g5.label: 5. Identity … also protection
g5.why: “Moreover” adds a further benefit of the clan system.

g6.label: 6. Wallace’s tactics vs Edward’s armies
g6.why: “In contrast” compares two opposite ways of fighting.

g7.label: 7. Opposed by Scots … went ahead
g7.why: “However” marks contrast: opposed by many, but it still happened.

g8.label: 8. Voted to remain … movement grew
g8.why: “Nevertheless” shows contrast: they voted to remain, yet the movement grew.

g4.label: 4. The age ___ they are

g5.label: 5. People ___ are under 30

g6.label: 6. young people ___ parents are in the business

g7.label: 7. the competition ___ they face
g7.why: A thing as the object — “which”/“that”, or omit it.

g8.label: 8. people ___ main income is from acting

g1.label: 1. By the time Drake set sail, he ___ to navigate
g1.why: The learning came before he set sail → past perfect: had + past participle.

g2.label: 2. When the Queen knighted him, Drake ___ wealthy
g2.why: He became wealthy before the knighting → past perfect: had become.

g3.label: 3. After Drake ___ his voyage, he returned
g3.why: “After” marks the earlier action → past perfect: had completed.

g4.label: 4. The soldiers were tired because they ___ all day
g4.why: The fighting happened before the tiredness → past perfect: had fought.

g5.label: 5. By 1588, the Spanish ___ the largest fleet
g5.why: Completed before 1588 → past perfect: had built.

g1.label: 1. When Henry VIII became king, …
g1.why: His father died before Henry became king → past perfect (had already died).

g2.label: 2. By the time the Armada arrived, …
g2.correct: Drake had warned the English fleet
g2.why: The warning came before the Armada arrived → past perfect.

g3.label: 3. After Drake …, the Queen rewarded him
g3.why: “After” marks the earlier action → past perfect: had returned.

g4.label: 4. The sailors were exhausted because they …
g4.why: No sleep came before the exhaustion → past perfect: had not slept.

g5.label: 5. Elizabeth was relieved because the Spanish …
g5.why: The failure to land came before her relief → past perfect.

g6.label: 6. Before Drake became famous, …
g6.correct: he had worked on merchant ships
g6.why: “Before he became famous” → the earlier job takes past perfect: had worked.

g7.label: 7. Drake told the Queen that he …
g7.why: Reporting an earlier completed action → past perfect: had captured.

g8.label: 8. By 1580, …
g8.correct: Drake had sailed around the world
g8.why: Completed by that date → past perfect: had sailed.

g7.label: 7. Many important decisions ___ in Washington

g1.why: Present passive: is + elected.

g2.label: 2. Parliament makes the laws →

g3.label: 3. Congress passed the law in 2020 →
g3.why: Past passive → was + passed.

g4.label: 4. They will hold an election next year →
g4.why: Future passive → will be + held.

g5.label: 5. The government has increased taxes →

g6.label: 6. Workers built the Capitol in 1800 →
g6.why: Past passive → was + built.

g7.label: 7. The King opens Parliament every year →
g7.why: Present passive → is + opened.

g8.label: 8. People speak English in both countries →

g1.label: 1. I ___ lived in Arizona
g1.why: The subject ‘I’ takes ‘have’ in the present perfect, not ‘has’.

g2.label: 2. She ___ visited the Grand Canyon
g2.why: He/she/it takes ‘has’ in the present perfect, not ‘have’.

g3.label: 3. We have known each other ___ 2019

g4.label: 4. They have lived here ___ ten years

g5.label: 5. Ellen Ochoa ___ inspired

g7.label: 7. He has worked in the same town ___ he was young

g8.label: 8. Lisa’s trip was the ___ holiday (good)
